_doc: FLOW-DIRECTIVE-1 (Rowan, 2026-11-12): every loop declares its typed inflows, outflows (with the binding each travels on) and its feedback path, so its outcomes return as signals that change its next output. Read by foundation/flows.py (python3 -m foundation flows --check). Fleet twin: QNFO/qnfo-workers _shared/flow-registry.js.
quote: How is this information flowing in? And what are we doing with it flowing out? And that applies to any workflow, any.

external_sources.ext.site_visits: readers of the public site (Cloudflare Web Analytics, returned by site.page)
external_sources.ext.post_engagement: replies, reposts and clicks on posts (returned by social.post)
external_sources.ext.owner_goals: IDEA.md and the owner's standing directives (instance manifest)

tick-heartbeat.feedback: verdicts and readings from its own past ticks re-rank the next pull

agent-executor.feedback: a red check or a reverted merge files an item the next tick takes

change-gate.feedback: failing checks return to the executor as items

merge-lane.feedback: lanewatch measures time to merge and files a stuck PR

site-deploy.feedback: page visits return through the dashboard snapshot as metric readings

social-post.feedback: engagement returns through the dashboard snapshot and steers the growth items

dashboard-snapshot.feedback: its readings are the measures every other loop is judged by

predict-verify.feedback: missed predictions lower trust and revert the change

trust-ledger.feedback: scope widens or narrows from verified outcomes

failure-audit.feedback: a detector that keeps firing escalates and files its own redesign

product-manager-pass.feedback: a growth item is kept only if its metric moved

plussing.feedback: accepted pluses are scored by the metric they named

issue-triage.feedback: priority rises with age and with capability gain

planning-roadmap.feedback: roadmap items close only on their metric
